info.title: consent-owner-resolver
info.description: The OwnerResolver API consumed by the consent-plugin. It answers two questions about a payload, WITHOUT ever seeing the requestor: does this data require a consent check, and who is its data owner. Written as JSON rather than YAML so the repository's own tests can parse it with the standard library and fail on drift - see internal/api/openapi_test.go.

post.summary: Resolve consent requirement and data owners for a payload
post.description: The request carries the data and its provenance, never the requestor. Ownership always comes from the data; `parties` exists only so the governing contract can be identified.

200.description: Resolved. `claims` is always a list, never null.

400.description: The request, or the payload inside it, could not be decoded.

401.description: AUTH_TOKEN is configured and the request did not present it.

422.description: Consent may be required but the owner could not be determined. The plugin applies its fail policy (deny by default). This NEVER means 'no consent needed'.

get.description: Unauthenticated by design: probes carry no credentials and this exposes no data.
Labels carry route, status and error class only - no request path and no owner - so this is safe to scrape without the shared secret.

200.description: Metrics in the Prometheus text exposition format.

bearerAuth.description: The optional shared secret (AUTH_TOKEN). When unset, /resolve is open and the network is the only control.

ResolveRequest.description: Unknown properties are ignored, so the plugin can add a field without waiting for a resolver deployment.

Resource.description: The data and its provenance. Deliberately carries no requestor identity.

service.description: Logical dataset/route id, configured on the plugin route.

path.description: Upstream request path - the primary handle for opaque data.

Parties.description: Identifies the governing contract ONLY. Never used to determine the data owner. `consumer` is required for `contract` matcher rules.

consumer.description: The requesting participant, e.g. the DID that issued the presented credential.

content.description: The payload; shape depends on `encoding`. Omitted for `none`.

consentRequired.description: Does this payload need a consent check?

claims.description: One entry per data item / subject. Always a list, never null.

ownerId.description: The data owner (subject), interpreted per ResolveResult.scheme.

participant.description: Optionally scopes the owner lookup to a participant.

dataResource.description: What this data is, in the vocabulary the consent is expressed in (Consent.data[].resource). Omitted for owner-level consent.

value.description: RFC6901 pointer; empty means the whole document. Absent for `whole`.

Error.description: Deliberately generic: the detail names the deployment's pointer configuration and goes to the log instead.
